situation:
You are the operations analyst at COPPER KETTLE SAUSAGE CO., a chain of twenty-six hot dog and sausage counters. The founder still owns the company, has run it for twenty years, and is preparing to sell it within the year. The founder (judge) has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

A limited-time bratwurst offer runs through the company app, which pushes it to customers who are already near a counter. The new point-of-sale system reports redemptions by counter and by hour, and those reports show the eight downtown counters absorbing almost all of them while the suburban counters see very few.

The downtown crews are working lunch rushes twice the size of last year's, holding the line times steady on a sandwich that takes longer to build. The suburban crews are quieter than they were before the offer launched, because the app is steering nearby customers to the counters that are already busiest. The quarterly bonus pool is split evenly by store, under a plan the founder wrote years ago.

Reweighting that pool by redemptions per counter would pay the downtown crews for the volume they absorbed and reward the work the reports can now measure, but it cuts the suburban crews' bonus for a shortfall the app's own targeting created, and those crews did nothing differently this quarter.

Leaving the even split and capping how many offers the app pushes to any one counter protects the suburban crews' bonus, but it throttles the offer where customers are actually redeeming it and lowers the sales the founder will show buyers. The founder (judge) wants your reading of what the reports say and a recommendation on the bonus. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) and owner of COPPER KETTLE SAUSAGE CO. Business background is the same as the situation above. You wrote the bonus plan that splits the pool evenly by store, you approved the limited-time bratwurst offer and the app targeting behind it, and you are preparing to sell the company within the year. You want the operations analyst to tell you what the redemption reports actually say and to recommend what to do about the quarterly bonus.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell a suburban crew their bonus is going down?
What would you say if they ask why the app sent the customers downtown?
